threads.body: [General] This branch still delegates to `warnDeprecated`, whose message says the boolean may be removed in the next minor release. The updated metadata promises removal in 3.0, so users receive conflicting timelines depending on which deprecated setting they use. Emit the same 3.0 warning used for the selector branch.

replies.body:
Addressed in 111a96e2a3a13378b119ab6615c3f78ab25a4a2e.

Analysis: The source-specific selectors and their older boolean forms share the 3.0 removal schedule because v3 preview already ignores them. The dedicated logging fallback now warns boolean users about that schedule without changing the generic warning for other experimental settings. The changelog still describes the v3-preview behavior but leaves the timeline to user-facing metadata and runtime warnings.

Upsides: Every deprecated structured logging fallback now gives users the same removal date. The changelog follows the repository deprecation policy.

Downsides: The dedicated resolver now contains warning text similar to the generic deprecation helper.

threads.body: Outside v3 preview, these fallback initializers still apply legacy boolean properties through the deprecated appender setters. At appender startup those setters emit warnings that say removal may happen next minor and recommend the source-specific selectors (`OpenTelemetryAppender.java:179-187,233-241,260-269`), contradicting this PR's 3.0/common-selector migration message. Route Spring property deprecations through a warning that names the common selector and correct timeline while preserving the library API's own deprecation semantics.

replies.body:
Addressed in c12695bca6f896eb836e2767bdac0f9fc99b5025.

Analysis: Spring now translates each legacy boolean property into an equivalent selector before configuring the appender. An enabled property includes `*`, while a disabled property excludes `*`. This preserves the property behavior and overrides appender XML without invoking the deprecated library setters. Spring emits its own 3.0 warning with the common selector replacement. Direct users of the deprecated appender API keep its next-minor warning and source-specific replacement.

Upsides: Spring users receive the correct timeline and migration target. The library API keeps its independent deprecation contract. Existing true, false, precedence, and appender XML behavior remains intact.

Downsides: The Spring initializer now translates legacy booleans into selector patterns instead of passing them through unchanged.

+  `otel.instrumentation.common.logging.structured-attributes.excluded`. MDC and logger-context
+  attributes remain separate and opt-in.

Analysis: Spring Boot shows these descriptions in configuration completion and hover help. Both selector properties named glob patterns without explaining the two supported wildcard characters. Adding the same syntax sentence used by the instrumentation documentation makes each IDE entry complete on its own.

Upsides: Spring users can configure both selectors correctly without opening separate documentation. The IDE metadata now matches the README and instrumentation metadata.

Downsides: The two property descriptions are slightly longer.
